claim: Stressful experiences potently activate kappa opioid receptors (κORs).
source: Stressful experiences potently activate kappa opioid receptors (κORs).
evidence: This is a general statement presented in the abstract without specific data or citations in this sentence, but it draws from established scientific knowledge in the field.

claim: κORs in the ventral tegmental area regulate multiple aspects of dopaminergic and non-dopaminergic cell function.
source: κORs in the ventral tegmental area regulate multiple aspects of dopaminergic and non-dopaminergic cell function.
evidence: This statement is presented as established knowledge without specific data in this sentence, drawing from the broader scientific literature.

claim: A single exposure to a brief cold-water swim stress induces prolonged activation of κORs at GABAergic synapses on rat VTA dopamine neurons.
source: Here we show that at GABAergic synapses on rat VTA dopamine neurons, a single exposure to a brief cold-water swim stress induces prolonged activation of κORs.
evidence: This is a primary finding of the study supported by experimental data presented in the manuscript.

claim: Stress-induced prolonged activation of κORs is mediated by activation of the receptor during the stressor followed by a persistent, ligand-independent constitutive activation of the κOR itself.
source: This is mediated by activation of the receptor during the stressor followed by a persistent, ligand-independent constitutive activation of the κOR itself.
evidence: This is a primary mechanistic finding supported by experimental data throughout the manuscript.

claim: The lasting change in κOR function is not seen at κORs at neighboring excitatory synapses.
source: This lasting change in function is not seen at κORs at neighboring excitatory synapses, suggesting distinct time courses and mechanisms of regulation of different subsets of κORs.
evidence: This is supported by experimental data presented in Figure 5 of the manuscript.

claim: Constitutive activity of κORs governs the prolonged reinstatement to cocaine-seeking observed after cold water swim stress.
source: We also provide evidence that constitutive activity of κORs governs the prolonged reinstatement to cocaine-seeking observed after cold water swim stress.
evidence: This is supported by behavioral data presented in Figure 6 of the manuscript.

claim: Acute and repeated stressors can escalate intake of addictive substances in animal models.
source: Animal models have shown that acute and repeated stressors can escalate intake of addictive substances (Piazza et al., 1990; Ramsey and Van Ree, 1993; Goeders and Guerin, 1994; Shaham and Stewart, 1994; Haney et al., 1995)
evidence: This claim is supported by multiple citations to previous research.

claim: Acute stress can reinstate drug seeking in animals that have undergone extinction training.
source: and that acute stress can reinstate drug seeking in animals that have undergone extinction training (Shaham et al., 1994, 1995; Conrad et al., 2010; Mantsch et al., 2016).
evidence: This claim is supported by multiple citations to previous research.

claim: Dopaminergic neurons of the VTA have emerged as a significant locus for the overlapping effects of drugs of abuse and stress.
source: In recent years, dopaminergic neurons of the VTA have emerged as a significant locus for the overlapping effects of drugs of abuse and stress (Polter and Kauer, 2014).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to previous work.

claim: Both acute stress and exposure to drugs of abuse induce a concomitant potentiation of excitatory synapses and loss of long term potentiation of inhibitory synapses.
source: Both acute stress and exposure to drugs of abuse induce a concomitant potentiation of excitatory synapses and loss of long term potentiation of inhibitory synapses (Ungless et al., 2001; Saal et al., 2003; Kauer and Malenka, 2007; Nugent et al., 2007; Chen et al., 2008; Niehaus et al., 2010; Polter and Kauer, 2014).
evidence: This claim is supported by multiple citations to previous research.

claim: A major mediator of stress-induced changes in inhibitory VTA synapses is the dynorphin/kappa opioid receptor (κOR) system.
source: A major mediator of stress-induced changes in inhibitory VTA synapses is the dynorphin/kappa opioid receptor (κOR) system.
evidence: This statement is presented as established knowledge based on the broader context of the field.

claim: κORs and their endogenous ligand, dynorphin, are found throughout the brain and have been highly associated with stressful, aversive, and dysphoric experiences.
source: κORs, and their endogenous ligand, dynorphin, are found throughout the brain and have been highly associated with stressful, aversive, and dysphoric experiences (Bruchas et al., 2010; Wee and Koob, 2010; Van't Veer and Carlezon, 2013; Crowley and Kash, 2015).
evidence: This claim is supported by multiple citations to previous research.

claim: κORs decrease the firing rate of dopamine neurons through activation of GIRK channels.
source: Within the VTA, κORs have a range of physiological effects. κORs decrease the firing rate of dopamine neurons through activation of GIRK channels (Margolis et al., 2003, 2006)
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to previous research.

claim: κORs inhibit excitatory synaptic transmission onto both dopaminergic and non-dopaminergic VTA neurons.
source: inhibit excitatory synaptic transmission onto both dopaminergic and non-dopaminergic VTA neurons (Margolis et al., 2005)
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to previous research.

claim: κORs reduce inhibitory synaptic transmission in a subset of dopamine neurons.
source: reduce inhibitory synaptic transmission in a subset of dopamine neurons (Ford et al., 2006)
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to previous research.

claim: κORs inhibit somatodendritic dopaminergic IPSCs.
source: and inhibit somatodendritic dopaminergic IPSCs (Ford et al., 2007).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to previous research.

claim: LTPGABA is induced via activation of nitric oxide synthase in the dopamine neuron, leading to nitric oxide (NO) release, and enhancement of GABA release through cGMP signaling.
source: LTPGABA is induced via activation of nitric oxide synthase in the dopamine neuron, leading to nitric oxide (NO) release, and enhancement of GABA release through cGMP signaling (Nugent et al., 2007, 2009).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to previous research.

claim: Acute stress blocks LTPGABA through activation of κORs.
source: More recently, we showed that acute stress blocks LTPGABA through activation of κORs
evidence: This claim is supported by previous work from the authors' lab.

claim: Preventing κOR activation via intra-VTA administration of the κOR antagonist, nor-binaltorphimine (norBNI), prevents stress-induced reinstatement of cocaine-seeking.
source: and that preventing this activation via intra-VTA administration of the κOR antagonist, nor-binaltorphimine (norBNI), prevents stress-induced reinstatement of cocaine-seeking (Graziane et al., 2013).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to previous research.

claim: A single exposure to stress leads to a loss of LTPGABA that lasts for at least five days and is mediated by persistent activation of VTA κORs.
source: Remarkably, a single exposure to stress leads to a loss of LTPGABA that lasts for at least five days and is mediated by persistent activation of VTA κORs (Polter et al., 2014).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to previous research.

claim: Treatment with the κOR antagonist after stress can rescue stress-induced reinstatement.
source: We have also shown that treatment with the κOR antagonist after stress can rescue stress-induced reinstatement.
evidence: This statement refers to previous work from the authors' lab.

claim: Bath application of the nitric oxide donor SNAP potentiates GABAergic synapses on dopamine neurons in the VTA.
source: As previously shown, bath application of the nitric oxide donor SNAP potentiates GABAergic synapses on dopamine neurons in the VTA, similarly to high-frequency stimulation of VTA afferents
evidence: This is supported by previous research and data shown in Figure 1A-B.

claim: SNAP-induced potentiation is blocked by single exposure to multiple drugs of abuse or acute cold-water swim stress.
source: this potentiation is blocked by single exposure to multiple drugs of abuse or acute cold-water swim stress (LTPGABA; Nugent et al., 2007; Niehaus et al., 2010; Graziane et al., 2013; Polter et al., 2014; Figure 1A–B).
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous research and data shown in Figure 1A-B.

claim: Blocking κORs with norBNI prevents and reverses the effects of acute stress on LTPGABA, even when administered several days after stress.
source: Our recent studies indicate that blocking κORs with norNBI prevents and reverses the effects of acute stress on LTPGABA, even when administered several days after stress (Graziane et al., 2013; Polter et al., 2014).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to previous research.

claim: Bath application of norBNI (100 nM) rescues SNAP-induced LTPGABA in slices from stressed animals.
source: Bath application of norBNI (100 nM) indeed allowed us to elicit NO-dependent LTPGABA in slices from stressed animals (Figure 1E)
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1E.

claim: Stress-induced activity of κORs in the VTA persists through brain slice preparation and recovery.
source: indicating that stress-induced activity of κORs in the VTA persists through brain slice preparation and recovery.
evidence: This is inferred from the observation that norBNI can rescue LTPGABA in slices from stressed animals.

claim: norBNI acts as an inverse or collateral agonist, and its interactions with the κOR can non-competitively inhibit further activity of κORs via activation of the JNK signaling cascade.
source: In addition to competing with agonists at the κOR agonist binding site, norBNI acts as an inverse or collateral agonist, and its interactions with the κOR can non-competitively inhibit further activity of κORs via activation of the JNK signaling cascade (Bruchas et al., 2007; Melief et al., 2010, 2011).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to previous research.

claim: LTPGABA remains blocked in slices pretreated with the JNK inhibitor SP600125 prior to norBNI application.
source: In contrast to the robust SNAP-induced potentiation observed in slices treated with norBNI alone, we found that LTPGABA remained blocked in slices pretreated with SP600125 (Figure 1F–H).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1F-H.

claim: Bath application of SP600125 does not interfere with expression of LTPGABA in slices from naïve animals.
source: Importantly, bath application of SP600125 did not interfere with expression of LTPGABA in slices from naïve animals or the loss of LTPGABA in slices from stressed animals (Figure 1—figure supplement 1A–B).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 1A-B.

claim: JNK activity has no role in LTPGABA induction or in the block of this plasticity by κORs.
source: Therefore, JNK activity has no role in LTPGABA induction or in the block of this plasticity by κORs, but is required for norBNI to rescue LTPGABA following stress.
evidence: This is inferred from the experimental data showing SP600125 does not affect LTPGABA induction or block.

claim: JNK activity is required for norBNI to rescue LTPGABA following stress.
source: Therefore, JNK activity has no role in LTPGABA induction or in the block of this plasticity by κORs, but is required for norBNI to rescue LTPGABA following stress.
evidence: This is supported by experimental data showing that JNK inhibition prevents norBNI rescue.

claim: 6β-naltrexol is a neutral antagonist that only inhibits agonist-stimulated κOR activity.
source: We treated such slices with either norBNI or 6β-naltrexol, a neutral antagonist that only inhibits agonist-stimulated κOR activity (Figure 2A–B; Wang et al., 2007).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to previous research and illustrated in Figure 2A-B.

claim: norBNI treatment rescues LTPGABA in slices from stressed animals.
source: While norBNI treatment rescued LTPGABA, bath application of the neutral antagonist did not reverse the stress-induced block of LTPGABA (Figure 2C–F).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2C-F.

claim: Bath application of 6β-naltrexol does not reverse the stress-induced block of LTPGABA.
source: While norBNI treatment rescued LTPGABA, bath application of the neutral antagonist did not reverse the stress-induced block of LTPGABA (Figure 2C–F).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2C-F.

claim: Bath application of 6β-naltrexol is sufficient to prevent depression of EPSCs onto VTA dopamine neurons induced by the κOR agonist U50488.
source: Bath application of 6β-naltrexol was sufficient to prevent depression of EPSCs onto VTA dopamine neurons induced by the κOR agonist U50488 (Figure 2—figure supplement 1B, Margolis et al., 2005)
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 1B and a citation.

claim: 6β-naltrexol does not have any effects on basal inhibitory transmission in slices from stressed or naïve rats.
source: 6β-naltrexol did not have any effects on basal inhibitory transmission in slices from stressed or naïve rats (Figure 2—figure supplement 1A).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 1A.

claim: The persistent block of LTPGABA is maintained by constitutive activation of κORs in the VTA rather than a prolonged increase in dynorphin release.
source: These results show that a κOR competitive antagonist cannot effectively rescue LTPGABA following stress, and suggest that the persistent block of LTPGABA is maintained by constitutive activation of κORs in the VTA rather than a prolonged increase in dynorphin release.
evidence: This is inferred from the experimental data showing differential effects of norBNI and 6β-naltrexol.

claim: Cells from animals treated with 6β-naltrexol before stress exhibit LTPGABA.
source: Consistent with our hypothesis, cells from animals treated with 6β-naltrexol before stress exhibited LTPGABA, while those treated one day after stress did not, similarly to the vehicle-treated animals (Figure 3B-F).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 3B-F.

claim: Cells from animals treated with 6β-naltrexol one day after stress do not exhibit LTPGABA.
source: Consistent with our hypothesis, cells from animals treated with 6β-naltrexol before stress exhibited LTPGABA, while those treated one day after stress did not, similarly to the vehicle-treated animals (Figure 3B-F).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 3B-F.

claim: Treating rats with norBNI one day after stress rescues LTPGABA.
source: In contrast, our previous studies have shown that treating rats with norBNI at the same time point after stress (one day) rescues LTPGABA (Polter et al., 2014).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to previous research.

claim: The persistent block of LTPGABA following acute swim stress is mediated by dynorphin-dependent activation of the κOR followed by a transition to dynorphin-independent constitutive activity of the receptor.
source: These data strongly support the idea that the persistent block of LTPGABA following acute swim stress is mediated by dynorphin-dependent activation of the κOR followed by a transition to dynorphin-independent constitutive activity of the receptor.
evidence: This is inferred from the experimental data showing differential effects of 6β-naltrexol timing.

claim: U50488 rapidly enters the CNS and is metabolized and undetectable in the brain by 24 hr after administration.
source: Upon injection, U50488 rapidly enters the CNS and is metabolized and undetectable in the brain by 24 hr after administration (Russell et al., 2014)
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to previous research.

claim: SNAP is unable to elicit LTPGABA in neurons from rats either one or five days after U50488 administration.
source: In contrast, SNAP was unable to elicit LTPGABA in neurons from rats either one or five days after U50488 administration (Figure 4C–F).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 4C-F.

claim: The time course of LTPGABA block after U50488 administration closely mirrors that of the in vivo block of LTPGABA following acute stress.
source: Notably, this time course closely mirrors that of the in vivo block of LTPGABA following acute stress (Polter et al., 2014).
evidence: This is a comparison to previous research supported by a citation.

claim: Bath application of the κOR agonist U69593 depresses the amplitude of glutamatergic EPSCs in both VTA Ih positive and Ih negative neurons.
source: Bath application of the κOR agonist U69593 has been reported to depress the amplitude of glutamatergic EPSCs in both VTA Ih positive (presumptive dopamine neurons) and Ih negative (presumptive non-dopamine neurons), and norBNI reverses this depression (Margolis et al., 2005).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to previous research.

claim: norBNI has no effect on EPSC amplitude in Ih-positive neurons in slices from either naïve or stressed animals.
source: NorBNI had no effect on EPSC amplitude in Ih-positive neurons in slices from either naïve or stressed animals (Figure 5A–C)
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 5A-C.

claim: norBNI does not increase EPSC amplitudes in VTA Ih-negative neurons in slices from either naïve or stressed animals.
source: and norBNI did not increase EPSC amplitudes in VTA Ih-negative neurons in slices from either naïve or stressed animals (Figure 5D–F).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 5D-F.

claim: The persistent constitutive κOR activation observed at GABAergic synapses after acute stress does not occur at all κORs, even within the VTA.
source: Therefore, the persistent constitutive κOR activation we observe at GABAergic synapses after acute stress does not occur at all κORs, even within the VTA.
evidence: This is inferred from the experimental data showing no effect of norBNI on excitatory synapses.

claim: There is a close association between κOR activation and stress-induced drug-seeking behavior.
source: Numerous studies from our lab and others have shown a close association between κOR activation and stress-induced drug-seeking behavior (McLaughlin et al., 2003; Redila and Chavkin, 2008; Land et al., 2009; Wee and Koob, 2010; Graziane et al., 2013; Zhou et al., 2013; Polter et al., 2014).
evidence: This claim is supported by multiple citations to previous research.

claim: Blocking κORs with norBNI reverses the modest but prolonged reinstatement of cocaine-seeking induced by swim stress.
source: We recently reported that blocking κORs with norBNI reverses the modest but prolonged reinstatement of cocaine-seeking induced by swim stress (Conrad et al., 2010; Graziane et al., 2013).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to previous research.

claim: norBNI rescue of reinstatement is seen even when norBNI is administered two hours after stress.
source: This rescue is seen even when norBNI is administered two hours after stress (Polter et al., 2014).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to previous research.

claim: After acute stress, vehicle-treated animals show a significant elevation of lever pressing compared to the final extinction session.
source: As previously shown, after acute stress, vehicle-treated animals showed a significant elevation of lever pressing compared to the final extinction session (Figure 6B).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 6B.

claim: Animals given norBNI 24 hr post-stress do not increase their lever pressing two days after stress.
source: In contrast, animals given norBNI 24 hr post-stress did not increase their lever pressing two days after stress (Figure 6B).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 6B.

claim: The neutral antagonist 6β-naltrexol does not prevent reinstatement.
source: Moreover, the neutral antagonist 6β-naltrexol did not prevent reinstatement, as 6β–naltrexol treated animals significantly increased lever pressing compared to the final extinction session (Figure 6B).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 6B.

claim: Persistent activation of κORs underlies the prolonged reinstatement induced by swim stress, mediated by constitutively active receptors rather than by long-term increases in the level of the endogenous ligand dynorphin.
source: These data suggest that while persistent activation of κORs underlies the prolonged reinstatement induced by swim stress, this is mediated by constitutively active receptors rather than by long-term increases in the level of the endogenous ligand dynorphin.
evidence: This is inferred from the behavioral data showing differential effects of norBNI and 6β-naltrexol.

claim: A single exposure to an acute stressor causes a lasting constitutive activation of VTA κORs that suppresses plasticity at inhibitory synapses correlated with stress-induced drug-seeking.
source: In this study, our data support the latter mechanism: a single exposure to an acute stressor causes a lasting constitutive activation of VTA κORs that suppresses plasticity at inhibitory synapses correlated with stress-induced drug-seeking (Figure 7).
evidence: This is a summary of the main findings supported by data throughout the manuscript and illustrated in Figure 7.

claim: Previous studies have demonstrated constitutive activity of κORs in cultured cells and in the rat brain.
source: While previous studies have demonstrated constitutive activity of κORs in cultured cells and in the rat brain (Wang et al., 2007; Sirohi and Walker, 2015)
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to previous research.

claim: This is the first demonstration of experience-induced changes in constitutive activity of κORs.
source: ours is the first demonstration of experience-induced changes in constitutive activity of these receptors.
evidence: This is a claim about the novelty of the current findings.

claim: GPCRs can adopt agonist-independent conformations that are constitutively active.
source: It is widely accepted that GPCRs can adopt agonist-independent conformations that are constitutively active (Seifert and Wenzel-Seifert, 2002; Sadée et al., 2005;Young et al., 2013 Meye et al., 2014).
evidence: This claim is supported by multiple citations to previous research.

claim: µOR and δOR have both been shown to exhibit constitutive activity.
source: In addition to κORs, the other members of the opioid receptor subfamily, µOR and δOR, have both been shown to exhibit constitutive activity (Wang et al., 1994, 2004; Chiu et al., 1996; Wang et al., 1999; Liu and Prather, 2001; Wang et al., 2007; Corder et al., 2013).
evidence: This claim is supported by multiple citations to previous research.

claim: κORs exhibit constitutive activity in heterologous expression systems.
source: κORs themselves have been shown to exhibit constitutive activity, both in heterologous expression systems (Becker et al., 1999; Wang et al., 2007)
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to previous research.

claim: κORs exhibit constitutive activity in the rat PFC.
source: and in the rat PFC (Sirohi and Walker, 2015).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to previous research.

claim: A decrease in fear and anxiety behaviors in rats after acute footshock has been reported that is reduced by post-shock norBNI.
source: A decrease in fear and anxiety behaviors in rats after acute footshock has also been reported that is reduced by post-shock norBNI, suggesting the possibility of constitutive κOR activation, although a high dose was required and the effect of norBNI was not compared to a neutral antagonist (Rogala et al., 2012).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to previous research.

claim: Signaling through the JNK pathway is thought to be responsible for the long-lasting non-competitive inhibition of the κOR.
source: Signaling through the JNK pathway is thought to be responsible for the long-lasting non-competitive inhibition of the κOR (Bruchas et al., 2007; Melief et al., 2010, 2011).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to previous research.

claim: Inhibition of LTPGABA by κORs is most likely mediated through the p38 or ERK MAPK pathways, or through activation of Gαi.
source: The failure of the JNK inhibitor to rescue LTPGABA indicates that inhibition of LTPGABA by κORs is not mediated by the JNK pathway, but instead most likely through one of the other pathways downstream of κORs, such as the p38 or ERK MAPK pathways, or through activation of Gαi (Bruchas and Chavkin, 2010; Iñiguez et al., 2010; Ehrich et al., 2015).
evidence: This is inferred from the experimental data and supported by citations to previous research.

claim: The block of LTPGABA by stress is unaffected by pre-stress administration of the µOR antagonist cyprodime.
source: Although 6β–naltrexol has equivalent affinity for µ and κ ORs, (Wang et al., 2007) our previous work has shown that the block of LTPGABA by stress is unaffected by pre-stress administration of the µOR antagonist cyprodime (Graziane et al., 2013).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to previous research.

claim: Previous exposure to a κOR agonist alone significantly increases constitutive activity of the receptor in a heterologous cell-culture system.
source: In a heterologous cell-culture system, previous exposure to a κOR agonist alone significantly increased constitutive activity of the receptor (Wang et al., 2007).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to previous research.

claim: Exposure to the µOR agonist morphine triggers an increase in constitutive activity of µORs in cultured cells or in intact animals.
source: In either cultured cells heterologously expressing µORs (Wang et al., 1994, 2000; Liu and Prather, 2001) or in intact animals (Wang et al., 2004; Shoblock and Maidment, 2006; Meye et al., 2012), exposure to the µOR agonist morphine triggers an increase in constitutive activity of µORs.
evidence: This claim is supported by multiple citations to previous research.

claim: Morphine-induced constitutive activity of µORs is regulated by calmodulin and protein kinases.
source: Morphine-induced constitutive activity of µORs is regulated by calmodulin and protein kinases.
evidence: This is presented as established knowledge from the field.

claim: Under basal conditions, calmodulin binding to the µORs prevents constitutive association with G-proteins.
source: Under basal conditions, calmodulin binding to the µORs prevents constitutive association with G-proteins. Following morphine exposure, calmodulin dissociates from the µOR, allowing constitutive activation (Wang et al., 1999, 2000).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to previous research.

claim: An intricate scaffolding complex regulates κOR signaling.
source: Although it is unknown whether calmodulin regulates the activity of κORs, an intricate scaffolding complex regulates κOR signaling (Bruchas and Chavkin, 2010)
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to previous research.

claim: Inflammatory pain increases constitutively active µORs in the mouse spinal cord, leading to hyperalgesia and cellular dependence.
source: However, it was recently reported that inflammatory pain increases constitutively active µORs in the mouse spinal cord, leading to hyperalgesia and cellular dependence (Corder et al., 2013).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to previous research.

claim: Activation of glucocorticoid receptors is required for the block of LTPGABA by stress.
source: Our prior work indicates that activation of glucocorticoid receptors is required for the block of LTPGABA by stress (Niehaus et al., 2010; Polter et al., 2014).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to previous research.

claim: The orexin-1 receptor attenuates κOR inhibition of cAMP production, but enhances recruitment of β-arrestin and p38 MAPK activation.
source: Additionally, it has been reported that the orexin-1 receptor attenuates κOR inhibition of cAMP production, but enhances recruitment of β-arrestin and p38 MAPK activation, and both effects are prevented by the JNK inhibitor SP600125 used in our study (Robinson and McDonald, 2015).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to previous research.

claim: Both orexin and dynorphin are co-released from hypothalamic projections to the VTA.
source: Both orexin and dynorphin are co-released from hypothalamic projections to the VTA (Chou et al., 2001; Muschamp et al., 2014; Baimel et al., 2015).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to previous research.

claim: LTPGABA is triggered by nitric oxide-mediated activation of cGMP-protein kinase G (PKG) signaling.
source: Our previous studies have shown that LTPGABA is triggered by nitric oxide-mediated activation of cGMP-protein kinase G (PKG) signaling (Nugent et al., 2007, 2009; Niehaus et al., 2010).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to previous research.

claim: The blockade of LTPGABA by stress is likely to occur in the presynaptic terminal between activation of guanylate cyclase and enhancement of GABAergic release.
source: Because an exogenous source of nitric oxide (SNAP) does not rescue potentiation following stress, the blockade is likely to occur in the presynaptic terminal between activation of guanylate cyclase and enhancement of GABAergic release.
evidence: This is inferred from the experimental observation that SNAP does not rescue LTPGABA after stress.

claim: κOR activation does not alter basal GABA release after cold water swim stress.
source: While it is possible that κOR activation generally depresses GABA release, our previous work (Graziane et al., 2013) found no change in mIPSC frequency following cold water swim stress. These data suggest that κORs do not alter basal GABA release.
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to previous research.

claim: LTPGABA is a heterosynaptic form of plasticity that can be triggered by a high-frequency tetanus that activates NMDAR-dependent activation of calcium-sensitive nitric oxide synthase.
source: LTPGABA is a heterosynaptic form of plasticity that can be triggered by a high-frequency tetanus that activates NMDAR-dependent activation of calcium-sensitive nitric oxide synthase (Nugent et al., 2007).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to previous research.

claim: GABAergic synapses on dopamine neurons strongly control their spontaneous firing.
source: As GABAergic synapses on dopamine neurons strongly control their spontaneous firing (van Zessen et al., 2012), the loss of LTPGABA is likely to prolong or enhance firing in response to salient stimuli.
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to previous research.

claim: The critical role of the VTA in reinstatement of drug seeking has been repeatedly underscored.
source: The critical role of the VTA in reinstatement of drug seeking has been repeatedly underscored (McFarland et al., 2004; Briand et al., 2010; Graziane et al., 2013; Mantsch et al., 2016)
evidence: This claim is supported by multiple citations to previous research.

claim: GABAergic synapses on VTA dopamine neurons powerfully regulate DA cell firing.
source: and within the VTA, GABAergic synapses on VTA dopamine neurons powerfully regulate DA cell firing (Tan et al., 2012; van Zessen et al., 2012; Polter and Kauer, 2014).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to previous research.

claim: In rats subjected to cold water stress, the firing rate of dopaminergic neurons remains elevated for several days afterwards.
source: Indeed, in rats subjected to the same cold water stress used in this study, the firing rate of dopaminergic neurons remains elevated for several days afterwards (Marinelli, 2007).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to previous research.

claim: A single dose of the κOR agonist, salvinorin A, has biphasic effects on reward function.
source: Interestingly, a single dose of the κOR agonist, salvinorin A, has biphasic effects on reward function: immediately after administration, rats exhibit an anhedonic increase in reward thresholds to intracranial self-stimulation. However, 24 hr after salvinorin A administration, rats exhibit decreased reward thresholds, indicating an increase in reward sensitivity (Potter et al., 2011).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to previous research.

claim: Dopamine neurons within the VTA exhibit physiological and functional heterogeneity that correlates with projection target.
source: The circuitry of the VTA is highly complex, and dopamine neurons within the VTA exhibit physiological and functional heterogeneity that correlates with projection target.
evidence: This is presented as established knowledge from the field.

claim: Activation of dopamine neurons that project to the nucleus accumbens has been shown to be rewarding in mice.
source: This may be significant for drug reward, as activation of these neurons has been shown to be rewarding in mice (Lammel et al., 2012).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to previous research.

claim: GABAB receptor-targeting neurons arise from the nucleus accumbens and regulate drug-induced behaviors.
source: Previous studies including more recent optogenetic approaches have suggested that GABAB receptor-targeting neurons arise from the nucleus accumbens and regulate drug-induced behaviors (Sugita et al., 1992; Cameron and Williams, 1993; McCall et al., 2017; Edwards et al., 2017).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to previous research.

claim: There is no LTPGABA at GABAB synapses on dopamine neurons.
source: However, our earlier work found no LTPGABA at GABAB synapses on dopamine neurons (Nugent et al., 2009)
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to previous research.

claim: norBNI does not prevent stress from potentiating excitatory synapses on dopamine neurons.
source: While considerable attention has been given to the role of LTP at excitatory synapses in the VTA, the κOR block by norBNI does not prevent stress from potentiating excitatory synapses on dopamine neurons (Graziane et al., 2013).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to previous research.

claim: κORs have shown promise as a potential drug target for substance use and mood disorders.
source: κORs have shown promise as a potential drug target for substance use and mood disorders (Bruchas et al., 2010; Van't Veer and Carlezon, 2013; Crowley and Kash, 2015)
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to previous research.

claim: In preclinical models, κOR antagonists have shown potential efficacy for depression and for compulsive and stress-induced drug use.
source: In preclinical models, κOR antagonists have shown potential efficacy for depression and for compulsive and stress-induced drug use (Bruchas et al., 2010; Wee and Koob, 2010).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to previous research.
